To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the European marine litter data management system, EMODnet Seabed Habitats, is a successful example for the implementation of a pan-European monitoring programme.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and implementation of a pan-European data management system for marine litter, and with the provision of data and data products that can be used to support the implementation of the Marine Strategy Framework Directive.

the following objectives: - to provide a framework for the collection, standardisation and dissemination of marine litter monitoring data at European scale, including data-sets from the European seas, the North-East Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea; - to develop data products and indicators that may be used for monitoring and assessment of marine litter at European scale; - to provide a basis for the development of a European marine litter monitoring network, and a global marine litter data management system.

(1) the collection and homogenisation of existing data-sets and the development of new data-sets; (2) the development and implementation of a common methodology for data harmonisation; (3) the development of a common data model for the storage and retrieval of data and data products; and (4) the development of an online platform for the dissemination of data-sets and products.

marine litter is a growing and global problem, with increasing impacts on human health and the marine environment.

marine litter is a global problem that is increasing in most parts of the ocean, and that the EMODnet Marine Litter data management plan is a key element in the development of a pan-European monitoring programme that will contribute to the global monitoring of this problem.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the main challenges in marine litter data management are: 1) the lack of harmonisation in sampling, monitoring and reporting; 2) the lack of a common data format; and 3) the need of a standardised approach to data processing, data validation, data quality control, data visualisation and data access.
the data management plan for the monitoring of marine litter at European level has been successfully developed and is now in the implementation stage.
we have been able to provide a solid data infrastructure that can be used as a baseline for future monitoring and research.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the EMODnet Marine Litter data management plan provides a robust and flexible platform that allows to collect, harmonise and provide access, to marine litter data at pan-European scale, and that can be easily adapted to future needs.
data harmonisation is a key step in the process, as it is a prerequisite for data integration.

a data management plan can be successfully implemented in the context of a network, and that it is possible to harmonise data and data products at pan-European scale, even if the data collection is done by different countries, using different methods and different protocols.
